summary.concentration: Focus and memory: retain information, ignore distractions, keep your head under pressure.
summary.conceal_reveal_object: Hide an object (including a weapon under clothes) or find a hidden one.
summary.lip_reading: Understand a conversation from lip movements at a distance.
summary.perception: Notice hidden things: clues, traps, people in hiding. Does not find objects hidden with Conceal/Reveal Object.
summary.tracking: Follow a trail using clues and tracks found earlier.
summary.athletics: Jumping, climbing, swimming, lifting, throwing. Includes thrown weapons.
summary.contortionist: Slip out of cuffs and restraints, squeeze into tight spaces.
summary.endurance: Withstand hardship, pain and fatigue: long stretches without food, sleep or water, harsh conditions.
summary.stealth: Move quietly, hide, avoid detection. Others look for you with Perception.
summary.accounting: Keep and audit books, find and hide fiddled accounts.
summary.animal_handling: Train, care for and work with animals.
summary.bureaucracy: Work the bureaucracy: know whom to talk to, speed up or stall paperwork.
summary.business: Running a business: managing staff, purchasing, sales, marketing, supply and demand.
summary.criminology: Investigate crimes: fingerprints, ballistics, crime scenes, police files.
summary.deduction: Draw non-obvious conclusions from a few clues, make a diagnosis.
summary.education: General knowledge, school level and above: reading, writing, math, history.
summary.gambling: Work out odds and play games of chance.
summary.language: Knowledge of a language. Pick the language each time you raise the skill.
summary.library_search: Find facts in databases, datapools and libraries.
summary.local_expert: Knowing an area: where to get things, where to hide, who runs what. Pick the area when you raise the skill, no bigger than one district.
summary.science: Scientific work: experiments, papers, testing hypotheses. Pick the field when you raise the skill (geology, math, physics, zoology, anthropology, biology, chemistry, history, ...).
summary.tactics: Direct a large-scale battle and anticipate the enemy.
summary.wilderness_survival: Survive in the wild: traps, firewood, hunting, shelters, fires.
summary.evasion: Dodge melee attacks. With REF 8 or more also ranged attacks and explosions.
summary.martial_arts: A martial art. Pick the form when you raise the skill (karate, taekwondo, judo, aikido); each form is learned separately.
summary.acting: Play a role, disguise yourself, fake emotions, imitate voices.
summary.play_instrument: Playing a musical instrument, singing included. Pick the instrument when you raise the skill.
summary.autofire: Keep on target in automatic fire despite recoil.
summary.handgun: Shooting pistols and other light handheld weapons.
summary.heavy_weapons: Heavy weapons, including grenade and rocket launchers.
summary.bribery: Bribe people: pick the approach and the sum.
summary.conversation: Draw information out of people without raising suspicion.
summary.human_perception: Read faces and body language, gauge mood, spot lies.
summary.interrogation: Extract information by force and pressure.
summary.persuasion: Persuade and influence people, individuals and crowds.
summary.personal_grooming: Grooming for attractiveness. Improves the odds when seducing or persuading.
summary.streetwise: Know where to get illegal goods, deal with criminals, stay out of trouble in bad areas.
summary.trading: Strike good deals with merchants and clients.
summary.wardrobe_style: Pick clothes and a look for the situation.
summary.basic_tech: Repair simple electronics and any item that no other tech skill covers.
summary.demolitions: Plant and defuse explosives, size the charge, spot explosives.
summary.electronics_security_tech: Complex electronics: computers, cyberdecks, security systems, bugs, laser traps. Repair, install, bypass.
summary.first_aid: First aid: keep the wounded alive and treat common critical injuries.
summary.forgery: Make and detect forgeries: documents, artwork, IP cards.
summary.paramedic: Stabilize the wounded and treat critical injuries that need no surgery. Surgery is for Medtechs only, through their role ability.
summary.pick_lock: Pick non-electronic locks and bypass non-electronic security.

reputation.title: Reputation
reputation.field_hint: −10 to 10, usually 0. Negative for cowardice and shameful deeds (p. 193).

how.name: How it works
how.detail: Awarded for deeds; a new deed replaces the old reputation if its level is higher. On meeting a stranger, roll d10: below the level means they have heard of you (p. 193).

negative.name: Negative reputation
negative.detail: For cowardice and the like. Those who heard of you are not impressed; it works against you (p. 193).

intimidation.name: Intimidation
intimidation.detail: Both roll COOL + Reputation + d10; reputation from cowardice counts as negative. A tie does nothing. The loser backs down or takes −2 to all actions against that opponent until they beat them (p. 194).

combat_turn.name: Turn and initiative
combat_turn.summary: Initiative = REF + d10. Each turn: 1 move and 1 action.
combat_turn.details:
A turn lasts about 3 seconds; a round is the turns of everyone in the fight.
Before the fight everyone rolls initiative (REF + d10) and lines up in descending order. A tie is rerolled. When the queue ends, a new round begins.
On your turn: 1 move (MOVE × 2, MOVE squares on the battle grid) and 1 action: attack, choke, draw or put away a shield, enter a vehicle, stand up, grab.

martial_arts.name: Martial arts: attack and damage
martial_arts.summary: 2 attacks per action, at least 1 point of the skill needed. Damage ignores half the armor and depends on BODY.
martial_arts.details:
Attack and special moves: DEX + style skill + d10 against the opponent's DEX + Evasion + d10, or the move's DV.
Damage ignores half of the target's armor (rounded up). Damage by BODY: up to 4 — 1d6, 5–6 — 2d6, 7–10 — 3d6, 11+ — 4d6.
A special move needs at least 1 point in that style. General moves are open to every style, each style has two of its own. Special moves cannot be made as an aimed shot unless stated otherwise.

other_damage.name: Fire, drowning, suffocation, electricity
other_damage.summary: Damage from fire, water, vacuum and electricity: what deals it and how it repeats.
other_damage.details:
Fire: at the end of each of your turns damage straight to HP until you put yourself out with an action; armor is not ablated, damage stacks. Weak (wood) 2, strong (gasoline) 4, deadly (thermite) 6.
Drowning: you can hold your breath for as many minutes as your BODY. After that, at the start of each turn damage equal to BODY straight to HP; it ignores armor and does not ablate it. Suffocation works the same way. In space an extra 1d6 damage to INT, REF and DEX at the end of the turn; at INT 0 the character is dead. Stat damage is undone once you can breathe again.
Electricity: 6d6 at once, armor blocks as usual. While you stay at the source the damage repeats at the end of each of your turns, starting with the next one.

attack_ranged.name: Ranged attack
attack_ranged.summary: Ranged attack: REF + weapon skill + d10 against the DV set by distance and weapon class.
attack_ranged.details: The attacker rolls REF + weapon skill + d10 against a DV set by distance and weapon class (the table at right). A defender with REF 8+ may dodge instead of using the table: DEX + Evasion + d10. The attacker wins; on a tie the defender wins. A hit deals damage minus armor.

attack_melee.name: Melee attack
attack_melee.summary: Melee: DEX + skill + d10 against DEX + Evasion + d10; 2 attacks per action.
attack_melee.details: The attacker rolls DEX + attack skill + d10 against the defender's DEX + Evasion + d10; the defender wins ties. The target must be within 2 m. Melee weapons have ROF 2 (two attacks per action), very heavy ones ROF 1. Damage ignores half of the armor (rounded up); brawling damage depends on BODY and does not halve armor.

attack_autofire.name: Autofire
attack_autofire.summary: Autofire: an action and 10 rounds, damage 2d6 × how much the DV was beaten by.
attack_autofire.details: Costs an action and 10 rounds (fewer is not allowed). Roll the Autofire skill against the DV from the autofire table. No aimed shots; a target with REF 8+ may dodge. On a hit, 2d6 damage is multiplied by the amount the DV was beaten by, capped by the weapon's multiplier (SMG 3, assault rifle 4). Two sixes cause a critical injury. Armor applies as usual.

attack_suppression.name: Suppressive fire
attack_suppression.summary: Suppressive fire: 10 rounds; targets within 25 m in the open roll WILL + Concentration against your REF + Autofire.
attack_suppression.details: Costs an action and 10 rounds. Everyone within 25 m along the line of fire, in sight and out of cover, rolls WILL + Concentration + d10 against your REF + Autofire + d10. Those who fail spend their movement to reach cover; if it is not enough they must Run to get as close to cover as they can.

attack_shotgun.name: Shotgun shell
attack_shotgun.summary: Shotgun shell: one attack against DV 13, hits everyone within 6 m in front of the shooter.
attack_shotgun.details: One ranged attack (REF + weapon skill + d10) against DV 13. On a hit, damage (rolled once) is dealt to everyone you can see in front of you within 6 m (3 squares). No aimed shots; targets with REF 8+ may dodge. Armor reduces damage as usual.

attack_explosives.name: Explosives
attack_explosives.summary: Explosion: a 10×10 m area around the target, damage rolled once; cover protects until destroyed.
attack_explosives.details: An explosion hits everyone (and the terrain) in a 10×10 m area (5×5 squares) centred on the target 2×2 m square. Damage is rolled once for all. If the attack check missed its DV, the GM decides where in that area it lands. A target with REF 8+ may dodge by rolling higher than the original check and leave the zone. Behind cover the blast cannot destroy, no damage passes; if the cover is destroyed, the target takes full damage.

attack_throw.name: Throwing
attack_throw.summary: Throwing an item or grenade: DEX + Athletics + d10, up to 25 m, DV as for a grenade launcher.
attack_throw.details: A ranged attack with DEX + Athletics + d10 up to 25 m; the DV comes from the grenade launcher row of the range table. A target that can dodge bullets can dodge a thrown item. A thrown melee weapon deals its damage (armor is not halved); a grenade deals what it would from a grenade launcher; improvised items deal damage as the GM decides.

attack_aimed.name: Aimed shot
attack_aimed.summary: Aimed shot: the whole action and −8 to the check; the effect depends on the area.
attack_aimed.details: A ranged or melee attack that takes the whole action and carries a −8 penalty to the check. On a hit an area effect is added. Head: damage that gets through head armor is doubled. Held item: if at least 1 damage gets through the armor, the target drops an item of your choice, which falls in front of them. Leg: if at least 1 damage gets through the armor, the target gets the critical injury Broken Leg (if they still have unbroken legs). Autofire and shotgun shells cannot be aimed.

attack_items.name: Items and reloading
attack_items.summary: Taking a ready weapon into a free hand and dropping it are not actions; stowing it, drawing a shield and reloading are.
attack_items.details: Taking a readily available weapon into a free hand is not an action. Dropping a weapon is not an action, but putting it away is. Drawing or stowing a shield is an action too. Reloading takes an action: the whole magazine is replaced, and its ammo must be of one type — types cannot be mixed.

attack_brawl.name: Brawling
attack_brawl.summary: Brawling: the Brawling skill, damage by BODY — 1d6 (≤4), 2d6 (5–6), 3d6 (7–10), 4d6 (11+).
attack_brawl.details: An attack with the Brawling skill. Damage depends on the attacker's BODY: 4 or less — 1d6, 5–6 — 2d6, 7–10 — 3d6, 11 or more — 4d6. With a cyberarm 2d6 applies already at BODY 4–6, and brawling damage is never below 2d6. The same skill is used to grapple and to resist a grapple. Unlike melee weapons, punches do not ignore half of the armor.

attack_grapple.name: Grapple
attack_grapple.summary: Grapple: DEX + Brawling + d10 against the target; both grapplers get −2 to all actions.
attack_grapple.details: An action to grab an opponent, snatch an item they hold, or break free. A free hand is required. The attacker and the target within reach roll DEX + Brawling + d10. The winner may grab the target or snatch an item with a free hand. Both grapplers get −2 to all actions; the defender cannot move on their own and is dragged along when the attacker moves. No two-handed weapons can be used in a grapple. The attacker can let go at any time without an action; to break the hold, the defender or another character spends an action on the same check against the attacker. A grapple is required for choking and throwing a person.

attack_choke.name: Choke
attack_choke.summary: Choke a grappled target: BODY damage ignoring armor; never drops to 0 HP; 3 rounds in a row — unconscious.
attack_choke.details: An action during a grapple: the held target takes damage equal to your BODY. The damage ignores armor and does not ablate it. If it would take the target to 0 HP, the target is left with 1 HP and falls unconscious. Choking the same target for 3 rounds knocks them unconscious regardless of HP.

attack_throw_person.name: Throwing a person
attack_throw_person.summary: Throw a grappled target to the ground: BODY damage ignoring armor; the grapple ends, the target is prone.
attack_throw_person.details: An action against a grappled opponent: throwing them to the ground deals damage equal to your BODY. The damage ignores armor and does not ablate it. The grapple ends (both are free of the −2), and the target is prone and cannot move until they spend an action to stand up. Throwing an item is a separate card.

combat_actions.name: Combat actions
combat_actions.summary: In your turn: 1 move and 1 action from the list — attack, grapple, choke, stabilize, use a skill, etc.
combat_actions.details: Main actions: move (MOVE × 2 m, on a grid MOVE squares); attack (melee or ranged); choke a grappled target; draw or stow a shield; get into a vehicle; stand up from prone; grapple; hold an action (name a place in the initiative queue or an event after which it triggers, the action itself and its target; within the round); human shield (use a grappled opponent); reload (the whole magazine, ammo of one type); run (an extra move, only if you already moved this turn); start a vehicle (take its MOVE and rise to the top of the initiative queue); stabilize a target (p. 222); throw a grappled opponent to the ground or throw an item; NET actions (p. 197); use an item (handling without a skill; taking a weapon into a free hand and dropping it to the floor take no action, stowing it in a belt does); use a skill (a small task takes an action, a large one several 3-second turns, the check is made at the end); vehicle maneuvering (concentrate on a dangerous maneuver).

combat_movement.name: Movement and splitting a turn
combat_movement.summary: Movement: MOVE × 2 m (MOVE squares on a grid, diagonals included); no moving while prone until you stand; movement can be split by an action.
combat_movement.details: Movement is MOVE × 2 meters or MOVE squares on a grid, diagonals included; on a grid you cannot stop between squares. While prone you cannot move until you spend the Stand Up action. Movement can be split: take your action in the middle of a move and continue afterwards. ROF 2 attacks split too: move, shoot, move, shoot; you can make one attack with each of two ROF 2 items at different points of the path. ROF 1 attacks take the whole attack action, but movement before and after them can be split. You cannot make more than two attacks per turn however many weapons you hold, and cannot attack with two ROF 1 weapons in one action. Swimming, climbing and running jumps cost 2 m of movement per meter (2 squares per square); a standing jump covers half the distance of a running jump. For falling and drowning see p. 180.

damage_taking.name: Taking damage
damage_taking.summary: Damage minus the armor SP of that location; the rest comes off HP; if anything got through, the armor SP drops by 1.
damage_taking.details: The attacker rolls damage. The SP of your armor at the hit location (the body unless a head shot was aimed) is subtracted from it, and the remainder is taken from your HP. If any damage got through (and only then), the armor at that location loses 1 SP until repaired. Poison and fire bypass armor.

wound_states.name: Wound states
wound_states.summary: Light — HP below max; serious — below half (−2 to all actions); mortal — below 1 HP (−4 to all actions, −6 MOVE).
wound_states.details: Each next threshold replaces the effect of the previous one. Lightly wounded: HP below full, no effect, stabilization DV 10. Seriously wounded: below half HP (rounded up), −2 to all actions, DV 13. Mortally wounded: below 1 HP, −4 to all actions, −6 MOVE (minimum 1); a Death Save is made at the start of each of your turns; every hit on a mortally wounded target causes a critical injury and raises the Death Save penalty by 1; stabilization DV 15 — the target returns to 1 HP but is unconscious for a minute. Dead: a failed Death Save, no coming back.

armor_rules.name: Armor and SP
armor_rules.summary: One SP per location — the highest worn; the REF/DEX/MOVE penalty is taken once, from the heaviest armor.
armor_rules.details: Armor is worn on the body and the head, and SP is tracked per location. The SP of several pieces on one location does not stack: the highest applies, and all worn protection on that location is damaged together. Heavy armor lowers REF, DEX and MOVE by the highest penalty among the pieces worn; it is applied once even with armor on both body and head, and can fully immobilize a character with MOVE 0.

critical_hits.name: Critical injuries
critical_hits.summary: Two sixes on the damage dice — a critical injury and 5 damage that bypasses armor.
critical_hits.details: If two or more of the damage dice of a melee or ranged attack show a 6, a critical injury is caused. Roll 2d6 on the table (body, or head for an aimed head shot) until you get an injury the target does not already have. Every injury has its effect and deals 5 bonus damage straight to HP: it does not damage armor and does not depend on the hit location. The injury and the bonus apply even if only part of the damage got through the SP. First aid and treatment — p. 223.

cover_rules.name: Cover
cover_rules.summary: You are in cover when fully behind something that can stop a bullet; cover has HP.
cover_rules.details: You are in cover if you are entirely behind something that can stop a bullet; if you can be seen, there is no cover. There is no partial cover: it either stops a bullet or it does not, and then it has no HP. An enemy can move to get a line of sight or destroy the cover (a grenade, for example). A 2 × 2 m section (1 square) has HP by material and thickness and takes damage like a target; at 0 HP the cover is destroyed, and excess damage is dissipated and does not reach those behind it (explosives are the exception, p. 174). Thin cover can be shifted a little, thick cover only with special equipment or at BODY 10+. Metal cannot be damaged by martial arts or brawling except with a cyberarm or at BODY 10+.

shields.name: Shields
shields.summary: A shield is mobile cover: it takes all the damage on its HP, but you cannot also dodge the attack.
shields.details: Drawing or stowing a shield is an action; the hand holding it is busy. While the shield has HP you are in cover. When a target you can see attacks you, you may shield yourself: you cannot dodge then, although the attacker can still miss. The shield takes all the damage on its HP; at 0 HP it is destroyed (a non-organic one can be repaired) and is no cover, but stays in your hand until you spend an action to drop it. Bulletproof shield: 10 HP.

human_shield.name: Human shield
human_shield.summary: A grappled enemy as cover: takes an action; he cannot dodge, and he does not protect from aimed head shots.
human_shield.details: If you hold an opponent in a grapple and the same hand is free (no shield), spend an action to use him as a human shield: while you hold him, you are in cover. You can cover yourself with him against a ranged attack not aimed at your head; he does not protect against aimed head shots (melee or ranged). A human shield cannot dodge ranged attacks, even with REF 8+. A hit damages him like any person. If he dies, he becomes a shield with HP equal to his BODY in life. To stop, end the grapple (no action); dropping the corpse takes an action, like other shields.

death_save.name: Death Save
death_save.summary: A mortally wounded character rolls a d10 at the start of the turn: up to BODY — alive; a 10 always fails; the penalty rises by 1.
death_save.details: If you are mortally wounded, roll a d10 at the start of each of your turns. A result within your BODY means you live and act as usual. A 10 automatically fails the save. Each save raises the penalty by 1 (the next one is made with +1), and it keeps building until you are stabilized to 1 HP; then it resets to its base value, which critical injuries raise. Fail once and you are dead. Every hit on a mortally wounded character causes a new critical injury and also raises the penalty by 1.

stabilization.name: Stabilization
stabilization.summary: TECH + First Aid or Paramedic + d10 against DV 10 / 13 / 15 (light / serious / mortal wound).
stabilization.details: Stabilizing is an action; roll TECH + First Aid or Paramedic + d10. The DV depends on the target's wound: light — 10, serious — 13, mortal — 15. You may stabilize yourself or another. A mortally wounded target gets 1 HP at once on success and is unconscious for exactly one minute; while unconscious they make Death Saves if mortally wounded again. To start natural recovery, the patient must be stabilized first.

natural_healing.name: Natural recovery
natural_healing.summary: After stabilization — BODY HP per full day of rest; break the rest and the day is lost and a new stabilization is needed.
natural_healing.details: A stabilized target regains HP equal to BODY for each full day of rest: spending most of the day at rest with only light activity, until at full HP. If the rest is broken, no HP is regained that day, the wounds reopen, and the target must be stabilized again to resume the process.

healing_skills.name: Healing skills
healing_skills.summary: Four skills: Cybertech, First Aid, Paramedic (×2), Surgery — each with its own range of tasks.
healing_skills.details: Cybertech is not used for stabilization: it repairs and "treats" injuries to implants (cyberlimbs, cybereyes). First Aid stabilizes and quickly removes the most common injuries; everyone has it, always trained to at least +2. Paramedic (×2) stabilizes and treats almost every critical injury except the most severe; everyone can learn it, but it is costly. Surgery treats even the deadliest injuries; only Medtechs have it, through their Medicine role ability.

injury_treatment.name: Treating critical injuries
injury_treatment.summary: First aid removes the effect until the end of the day (1 minute, can be done on yourself); treatment removes it for good (4 hours, not on yourself).
injury_treatment.details: There are two ways to deal with a critical injury. First aid removes the effect until the end of the day; an attempt takes a minute and you can help yourself. Treatment removes the effect permanently; each attempt takes four hours and you cannot treat yourself. The skills and DVs needed are in the injury table; the most severe injuries need Surgery. If the injury hits a body part replaced by an implant (cyberarm, cyberleg, cybereye), the effect and bonus damage still apply, but it can be repaired with Cybertech instead of First Aid, Paramedic or Surgery, at the same DV and in the same time.

hospital_costs.name: A hospital visit
hospital_costs.summary: You pay only for the highest DV of stabilization or treatment of the visit: 50 / 100 / 500 / 1000 eb; a bed is 100 eb a night.
hospital_costs.details: When you check into a hospital, you pay only for the highest stabilization or treatment DV needed during the visit: DV 10 — 50 eb (Costly), DV 13 — 100 eb (Premium), DV 15 — 500 eb (Expensive), DV 17 and up — 1000 eb (Very Expensive). Everything else needed for recovery is included. You normally leave the same day; a bed costs 100 eb (Premium) a night. An unpaid bill can be put off until the start of next month, but collection agents come for non-payers.

medical_replacements.name: Spare parts and the bodybank
medical_replacements.summary: A lost body part is replaced by a clone or a medical-grade implant (50 eb): no slots, no humanity loss.
medical_replacements.details: If a body part is lost to a critical injury, the hospital replaces it with a clone grown from the patient's own tissue or a medical-grade cyberimplant. Cloned limbs are included in the hospital visit price (the Bodybank). Buying your own limb to keep in storage "just in case" costs 50 eb (Costly). A medical-grade implant restores full function and nothing else: it has no upgrade slots and does not count as a cyberweapon. It causes no humanity loss. A patient who wants a full cybernetic replacement first pays for the Treatment of the injury, then for the implant itself.

cyberware_install.name: Installing cyberware
cyberware_install.summary: Medtech only: Mall — DV 13, 100 eb; Clinic — DV 15, 500 eb; Hospital — DV 17, 1000 eb.
cyberware_install.details: Only a Medtech with Surgery can perform the installation, and not on themselves unless the installation site is a Mall. DV and price depend on the site: Mall — DV 13, 100 eb (Premium); Clinic — DV 15, 500 eb (Expensive); Hospital — DV 17, 1000 eb (Very Expensive). Extracting cyberware from a corpse takes Surgery against the same DV. A failure destroys the implant. The patient bears the humanity loss of the installation.

humanity.name: Humanity
humanity.summary: HUM = EMP × 10; when the tens digit of HUM changes, EMP drops to the tens of HUM.
humanity.details: Empathy is a STAT, and each point of EMP gives 10 points of Humanity: with EMP 5 you have 50 HUM. Humanity is lost mostly by installing cyberware. Whenever the tens digit changes (for example from 50 to 46), EMP drops to the tens of HUM (from 5 to 4). Losing humanity means losing empathy for others and the instinct for self-preservation; the extreme form is cyberpsychosis. Replacing a lost body part with a clone or a medical-grade implant does not reduce humanity.

humanity_trauma.name: Psychic trauma
humanity_trauma.summary: Severe events cost humanity: 1d6 for a one-off shock, 2d6 for prolonged stress.
humanity_trauma.details: Humanity is lost not only to implants but also to strong, traumatic events; the GM decides. A traumatic physical event (torture) — 1d6. A traumatic psychological event (you witness a particularly horrible death or mutilation) — 1d6. Long-term psychic stress (abduction, imprisonment, prolonged abuse) — 2d6. Long-term stressors in your life (facing starvation, living in a war zone, a month of constant danger) — 2d6.

therapy.name: Therapy
therapy.summary: A week of therapy, a Medical Tech check: addiction — DV 15; standard — DV 15, 2d6 HUM; extreme — DV 17, 4d6 HUM.
therapy.details: Therapy is run by a Medtech (the Medical Tech skill from the Medicine ability): a week during which doctor and patient do nothing else, ending with a roll against the therapy DV. A failure wastes the week. A Medtech cannot treat themselves. Addiction: 1000 eb, DV 15, materials worth 500 eb; clears one addiction, but for a year after therapy you automatically fail attempts to resist the secondary effect of that same source. Standard humanity loss: 500 eb, DV 15, materials worth 100 eb; restores 2d6 HUM. Extreme: 1000 eb, DV 17, materials worth 500 eb; restores 4d6 HUM. Humanity cannot be fully restored without removing cyberware: each installed piece lowers the maximum by 2, each piece of borgware by 4, and implants with zero impact do not reduce it. A hospital night costs 100 eb.

skill_checks.name: Skill checks
skill_checks.summary: STAT + skill + d10 against the task's DV, or against the opponent's STAT + skill + d10; the defender wins ties.
skill_checks.details: When the outcome is uncertain, make a skill check. There are two ways. Opposed: you roll STAT + skill + d10 against the opponent's matching STAT + skill + d10; their result is the DV, and the defender wins ties. Against difficulty: the GM rates the task on the DV table, and you roll STAT + skill + d10 and must beat the DV. STAT + skill together are called the skill total. If a task is obviously easy, no roll is needed.

task_dv.name: Task difficulty (DV)
task_dv.summary: DV: simple 9, everyday 13, difficult 15, professional 17, heroic 21, incredible 24, legendary 29.
task_dv.details: The GM picks a DV from the table. Simple — 9 (most people can do it without thinking). Everyday — 13 (most people without special training). Difficult — 15 (hard without training or natural talent). Professional — 17 (needs real training, professional level). Heroic — 21 (a feat only the best of the best manage, star level). Incredible — 24 (a huge feat; you become one of the best of your class). Legendary — 29 (people will talk about it for years).

roll_crits.name: Critical success and failure
roll_crits.summary: A natural 10 on the d10 — roll another d10 and add it; a natural 1 — roll another d10 and subtract it; repeats do not chain.
roll_crits.details: If the d10 shows a 10, it is a critical success: roll another d10 and add it to the first roll; a second 10 does not give another critical success. If it shows a 1, it is a critical failure: roll another d10 and subtract it from STAT + skill + the first roll; a second 1 does not give another critical failure. Despite the names, a character can succeed after a critical failure, and a high DV can beat a critical success.

roll_modifiers.name: Roll modifiers
roll_modifiers.summary: The GM subtracts a penalty: poor light and a first attempt −1; hard task, no tools, stress −2; exhaustion, intoxication, stealth, smoke −4.
roll_modifiers.details: External conditions give a modifier subtracted from the roll; they stack. Examples: night or poor light −1; never done it before −1; a complicated task −2; no tools or parts −2; slept badly the night before −2; stressful conditions −2; exhausted −4; drunk or on drugs −4; having to act covertly −4; smoke or darkness hampering the task −4. Positive modifiers come from gear, implants, abilities and drugs.

check_options.name: Retries, related skills, time, luck
check_options.summary: No repeats without a change; related skill +1, 4× time +1, no skill — only the STAT; Luck +1 per point.
check_options.details: After a failure you cannot retry until your odds improve: more time, a better tool, or a related-skill check. Related skill: at the GM's discretion a good roll in another skill (possibly by another character) gives +1 to the next attempt; the bonus applies once and bonuses from different related skills do not stack. Extra time: +1 if the task takes 4 times longer. No skill: roll only the STAT + d10. Luck: before a roll you may spend Luck points (their number equals LUCK, refreshed at the start of each session), each giving +1.

scale_and_movement.name: Distance, time and speed
scale_and_movement.summary: Meters and yards are equal; a square is 2 m; reach is 2 m; a turn is ≈ 3 seconds; walking 4 km/h, running 11 km/h.
scale_and_movement.details: All distances are measured in meters and yards (treated as equal). On a grid one square is 2 meters. Reach is 2 m: you can touch what is within arm's length and need a tool or weapon for the rest. You can interact with what you can see with the naked eye or through a scope. There are three scales of movement: narrative (speed in km/h), figurative (comparing the MOVE of two moving bodies) and literal (meters in combat: MOVE × 2 m or MOVE squares). Human speed per the book: walking 2.5 mph (4 km/h), running 5 mph (11 km/h, as printed). Time: roleplay time runs as in life; combat time is divided into turns of ≈ 3 seconds, and a round is a turn of every participant.

weapon_quality.name: Weapon quality
weapon_quality.summary: Poor quality jams on a critical failure, excellent quality gives +1 to attack; the price depends on the base one.
weapon_quality.details:
Melee and ranged weapons come in three qualities: poor, standard and excellent. Exotic weapons are always standard quality unless stated otherwise.
Poor: on a critical failure of the attack (a 1 on the die) the weapon breaks down and you must spend an action to clear the fault (no check needed).
Excellent: +1 to the attack check.
Price: standard 50 eb — poor 20, excellent 100; standard 100 eb — poor 50, excellent 500; standard 500 eb — poor 100, excellent 1000.

weapon_mods_rules.name: Weapon modifications
weapon_mods_rules.summary: A non-exotic ranged weapon has 3 modification slots; the same modification twice does not stack.
weapon_mods_rules.details:
Every non-exotic ranged weapon has 3 modification slots. You can fit several different modifications while slots last. The same modification installed twice does not add its effect twice. A modification is made for a certain type of weapon and cannot simply be moved to a weapon of another type.
The list of modifications and the magazine table are in the reference.

ammo_rules.name: Ammunition
ammo_rules.summary: Each weapon type needs its own ammunition; grenades and rockets are sold one by one, the rest by 10.
ammo_rules.details:
Ammunition comes in several kinds: cartridges (for pistols, the shotgun and rifles), shot, arrows, grenades and rockets. Each type of weapon needs its own kind.
Grenades and rockets are sold one by one, other ammunition by 10. A grenade can be thrown or loaded into a grenade launcher.
Special ammunition types (armor-piercing, incendiary and so on) are in the reference.

price_categories.name: Prices and price categories
price_categories.summary: Eight categories from Cheap (10 eb) to Super Luxury (10,000 eb and up); without a Fixer you can buy nothing above Premium.
price_categories.details:
Everything bought in the game belongs to one of eight price categories that set the market price: Cheap 10 eb, Everyday 20, Costly 50, Premium 100, Expensive 500, Very expensive 1000, Luxury 5000, Super luxury from 10,000 eb.
Without an experienced Fixer or their Night Markets you can only buy items up to Premium. Without a Fixer you can forget about a discount, and an Expensive item cannot be bought at all.

INT.name: Intelligence
INT.summary: How smart you are: quick wits, awareness, perception, the ability to learn.

WILL.name: Willpower
WILL.summary: Determination, resistance to danger and stress, endurance of hardship. Affects HP.

COOL.name: Cool
COOL.summary: Making an impression and influencing people, conduct in social situations.

EMP.name: Empathy
EMP.summary: Attitude to other people, care for them, taking their view into account. Softens the effects of cyberpsychosis.

TECH.name: Technique
TECH.summary: Handling tools and devices. Not the same as Reflexes.

REF.name: Reflexes
REF.summary: Reaction time and coordination for aiming and throwing. Affects hitting with ranged weapons.

LUCK.name: Luck
LUCK.summary: Points that raise a roll. They refill at the start of the next game session.

BODY.name: Body
BODY.summary: Size, stamina, the ability to survive and stay conscious. Affects HP.

DEX.name: Dexterity
